summary: The City of Marlow Springs wants a mechanical service contractor to do scheduled preventive maintenance and on-call repair of HVAC equipment at eleven city buildings for three years from July 1, 2027, with up to two one-year renewals. The City has budgeted about $95,000 per year. Proposals must be uploaded to the City's bid portal as a single PDF by 4:00 p.m. on Thursday, March 11, 2027.

notes.text: The $95,000 is an approximate budget per year, not the value of the whole contract. The term is three years, and the City may renew for up to two more one-year terms, so the contract could run three to five years.

The text says the contractor must hold a Utah S350 HVAC Contractor license but does not say whether it must be held when the proposal goes in or only when the contract starts, and it does not ask for a copy in the proposal. I read it as a requirement on the firm that wins; a firm without the license should ask before proposing. Every technician assigned to the contract must also hold EPA Section 608 certification.

A certificate of insurance must be in the proposal itself, not only after award. The required coverage is set out in Exhibit D, which is not part of the text I was given, so I cannot say what the amounts are. Exhibits A, B and C are also referred to but not included.
On-call repair response is required every day of the year: a technician on site within four hours during business hours and within eight hours at other times. The text does not define business hours.

The text says any qualified firm may submit a proposal; I read that as open to all with no set-aside, though it does not use those words. It says there is no pre-proposal meeting; site visits may be arranged by appointment, but it does not say with whom or by when. Questions are due by email, yet this section gives no address; the only one in the text is bids@marlowsprings.example in the contact section. The address of the bid portal is not given.
